opportunities.title: Disaster response tools are not software. They are social contracts.
opportunities.text: Disaster response tools are not software. They are social contracts. The failure of a tool during a crisis is rarely a failure of the logic alone. It is a failure of the translation layer between the person who needs a specific outcome and the person who writes the code to achieve it. When requirements are gathered in a vacuum, the resulting software is not a solution. It is a monument to what the developer assumed the user knew. Software isn't a finished object to be handed over to a department. The development lifecycle has to absorb the operational reality of the end-user, or the tool just becomes another piece of redundant infrastructure that fails when the lights go out. A Humanities and Social Sciences Communications 2026 study highlights this exact friction. By using NVivo software
